content.thinking:
I'm trying to phrase the symptom simply, without numbers, capturing that purchases stopped being confidently categorised and many fell into a generic bucket instead.

For the cause, I'm checking the evidence: the shop was running categoriser model v2 instead of v1, confirmed across all three replicas and the deploy logs. I'm also ruling out the earlier deploy as a trigger since metrics before that point remained healthy right up until the actual onset time, and no flag changes occurred around then either.

The real trigger was the deploy that switched categoriser.model from v1 to v2 in the values file with no source code change — confirmed by the diff and corroborated by the rollback restoring healthy behavior. As for why v2 caused lower confidence, I'm tracing it to a case-sensitivity issue: the categorise function passes words through without lowercasing, so capitalized words miss matches against the lowercase vocabulary and get miscategorized as low-confidence, with the source code itself unchanged between versions.

The risk remains live since the repository's production config still names v2, so re-enabling sync would reintroduce the same failure without any code change. As a contributing factor, there doesn't seem to have been a check ensuring the new model version got input in the format it expected, or a test of categorisation under v2 with capitalised titles before the config shipped — something that could have caught this before deploy.

A second factor: the switch went straight to all three replicas with no canary or staged rollout, so the failure hit everything at once instead of being contained; I'd propose gating model changes behind a partial rollout with a confidence threshold. And a third factor is that nobody got paged — the alert doesn't page.

For detection, Argus caught it six minutes after onset and handled it, so paging wasn't actually necessary to shorten the incident, so I'll skip that as a contributing factor rather than something that went wrong.

For action items, I'm drafting two preventive measures: a pre-deploy check that runs a sample of real titles through any new model version and blocks the change if confidence drops, and a staged rollout mechanism for categoriser.model changes that pulls back automatically if confidence falls. I'm also noting the immediate fix of reverting categoriser.model in the production values file back to v1.

I'm considering whether to add a mitigation item ensuring AI-3's repository sync doesn't reintroduce the broken version before the fix merges, since AI-3's own description implies this requirement without explicitly tracking it. I'm also weighing whether to flag that the categorising.py comparison only checked against the previous revision rather than main, but deciding to leave that as an assumption rather than a formal action item. For things that went well, I want to credit Argus for catching the issue quickly.

Got-lucky seems empty too — no failed requests or lost sales isn't luck, and the rollback working because every version ships in the image is by design, not chance. For assumptions, I'm checking that F1 runs against main and that the file matches what D1 shows, with harm to users inferred from low-confidence purchases being filed under "General." I'll keep figures as placeholders like "many" rather than specific numbers.

Ruling out the flag-change theory: no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before, phrased with placeholder tokens for the time window. For v2, I'm noting that as of the known timestamp, all replicas ran the same revision. Earlier deploy is ruled out since the metrics pulled a few minutes back from the reference time still showed the series healthy.

action_items.item: Add a pre-deploy check for any change to `categoriser.model` in deploy/values-production.yaml. It runs a sample of real purchase titles, with their case as written, through the newly selected model and blocks the change if its confident share falls below the current model's.
Roll out changes to `categoriser.model` to part of the replicas first, and stop the rollout automatically if the share of confidently categorised purchases falls.

Set `categoriser.model` in the repository's deploy/values-production.yaml back to v1 until a revision carrying the lowercasing fix is deployed, so that turning automatic sync back on does not put v2 back.

causal_chain.step: From the onset at {T6.2}, far fewer purchases got a confident category. The share of purchases categorised confidently fell from {series_before} before the onset to an average of {series_while_broken}, and to {series_at_worst} at its worst. The error rate stayed at {errors_while_broken}, against {errors_before} before, so requests kept succeeding but many purchases were left without a confident category.

The shop was categorising purchases with model v2 instead of v1. As of {T10.1}, all {T10.2} replicas ran revision 7c3ca00c7528df68d533f6e87acd4f23a55ab342. That revision's production values file sets `categoriser.model: v2`.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision d268103129978816ce705c50c14cd42c7c5fe46e at {P1.1}. The metrics read back {T5.2} minutes from {T4.2} show the service healthy with that revision in place, at {series_before}, until the onset at {T6.2}.
A feature-flag change. The flag provider's history showed {T14.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T14.3} hour before {T14.4}.

causal_chain.step: The deploy of revision 7c3ca00c7528df68d533f6e87acd4f23a55ab342 at {P2.1} changed `categoriser.model` from v1 to v2 in deploy/values-production.yaml. That is the only change its diff shows: no source file changed. Rolling the deployment back off this revision brought the service back from the incident's level, and the action was judged confirmed.

Model v2 likely misses capitalised words. In the source Code-Fix read, `categorise()` passes the model `title.split()` with each word's case unchanged. `CategoriserModel.predict` lowercases words only when `lowercases_its_input` is true, which v1 sets and v2 does not. v2's vocabulary was built from lowercased titles, so under v2 a capitalised word misses the vocabulary and the purchase is filed under "General" with confident=False, without an error. This reading is of main, and nothing ran it. D1 shows the revision changed no source file compared with the revision before it.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A configuration change moved the shop to a newer model for sorting purchases into categories. That model likely expects every word in lowercase, but the shop hands it words exactly as written, so it could not confidently place many purchases.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that runs real purchase titles, with their case as written, through a newly selected model version before a values change that switches models ships to production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The drop in confident categorisation under v2 would likely have shown up before the deploy, and the switch would not have reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The model switch went to every replica at once. As of {T10.1}, all {T10.2} replicas ran the new revision, and no staged or partial rollout of the model change was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only some purchases would have been categorised by v2 before the drop was noticed, and the rollout could have been stopped before it reached the whole shop.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator tied the drop to the model switch in revision 7c3ca00c7528df68d533f6e87acd4f23a55ab342, and Argus rolled the deployment back {T17.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed the rollback had brought the service back from the incident's level {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Because every model version ships in the image, moving back off v2 was a rollback rather than a rebuild (S1).

Code-Fix opened draft pull request #353 {T22.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised. It proposes lowercasing each word in `categorise()` before it reaches the model, plus tests for capitalised titles under v2.

input.root_cause: Model v2 does not lowercase the words it is given (v1 does), because v2 was trained on a vocabulary built from lowercased titles. The shop's `categorise()` passes it `title.split()` with the case of each word unchanged. Any capitalised word misses v2's vocabulary, and the purchase is filed under "General" with confident=False. Nothing raises an error or slows down.
input.still_at_risk: The shop's code still hands the model words with their case unchanged, and the repository's production configuration still selects model v2 (S1). Anything that deploys that configuration again would likely bring back the same drop in confident categorisation.
input.symptom: Many purchases were filed without a confident category, while requests kept succeeding
